## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13420: Session history FTS search — searchable session history via indexed command bar (HIGH ~10h)

- **What**: Kilocode added searchable session history via FTS-indexed command bar (Cmd/Ctrl+P). Replaces sidebar search dialog that eagerly loaded all sessions via `loadAllSessions()` upfront (memory spike on large histories). New architecture: session index populates on first search (background indexer scans session files), queries run server-side FTS (SQLite FTS5 or equivalent) with rank-based scoring, results pass through command bar with `shouldFilter: false` passthrough so server ranks are preserved instead of re-sorted by cmdk fuzzy matcher. Index eviction: failed restoration sessions (corrupted/missing files) evicted from search results, deleted sessions suppressed during reconciliation (delete event marks session as suppressed, reconciliation preserves suppression flag). Command bar shows timestamp, title, model, workspace for each result.
- **Why**: Loading all session JSON files upfront is slow (100+ sessions = multi-second freeze) and memory-intensive. FTS search with lazy loading scales to thousands of sessions without blocking the UI.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13420 (feat: add searchable session history)
- **Category**: command (session management / search)
- **Size**: HIGH (~10h — Alexi TUI history.ts L1-237 lists recent sessions via filesystem scan (`fs.readdirSync` on `~/.alexi/sessions/`, sort by mtime, display top 20), no FTS index, no search, no ranking. Implementing FTS-indexed session search requires: (1) session index schema (session id, title, model, workspace, timestamp, message count, tags), (2) background indexer (watch `~/.alexi/sessions/`, parse JSON, upsert into FTS table on create/update, delete from index on remove), (3) FTS query endpoint (accept search string, run FTS5 MATCH, rank by bm25, return top N results with metadata), (4) TUI search UI (add search prompt to history view, query FTS endpoint on input, display ranked results with highlight, select to load session), (5) index reconciliation (evict failed restorations, suppress deleted sessions). Pattern is CLI-portable. SQLite FTS5 is available in Node.js via better-sqlite3 (already a dependency in some Cline workflows). Moderate implementation complexity but high user value for large session histories).

#### 2. Cline #13639: Remote MCP connect timeout — bounded connect budget for remote MCP clients (MODERATE ~4h)

- **What**: Cline remote (SSE/streamable HTTP) MCP connects ran on session.create critical path without connect timeout, inheriting 60s default HTTP request timeout. Unreachable server (network down, DNS failure, server offline) spent full 60s attempting connection, stalling session.create past hub's 30s deadline and tearing down the session — interactive TUI exited, one-shot runs failed. Stdio MCP servers already had bounded initialize budget for this reason. Fix: remote clients now have 10s default connect budget (same as stdio initialize timeout), overridable via explicit `timeout` (or `timeoutMs`) config field in mcp-servers.json per server. Budget covers transport handshake + initialize RPC. Transient failures (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, socket hang up) still retry with exponential backoff within the budget.
- **Why**: Unreachable remote MCP server should fail fast (10s), not block session creation for 60s and tear down the session.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13639 (Fix CLI crash when a remote MCP server is offline but enabled)
- **Category**: mcp (client / timeout)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~4h — Alexi mcp/client.ts L1-498 has NO per-transport connect timeout for remote clients. `connectMCPServer` L89-170 dispatches to stdio/sse/streamable transports, stdio has 30s initialize timeout (mcp/transports/stdio.ts L65 `initializeTimeoutMs: 30000`), but sse/streamable transports (mcp/transports/sse.ts, mcp/transports/streamable.ts) have NO explicit connect timeout — inherit default HTTP client timeout (Node.js http.request default is no timeout, fetch default is implementation-dependent). Unreachable remote server would stall indefinitely or until global timeout. Implement: (1) add `connectTimeoutMs` field to RemoteMCPServerConfig (mcp/types.ts), default 10000, (2) pass timeout to sse/streamable transport constructors, (3) wrap transport.connect() in Promise.race with timeout, (4) reject with descriptive error on timeout, (5) honor explicit `timeout` or `timeoutMs` config field per server in mcp-servers.json. Reuse existing `initializeTimeoutMs` budget pattern from stdio transport).

#### 3. Kilocode #13614: Global rules path discovery — add ~/Cline/Rules fallback for headless installs (MODERATE ~3h)

- **What**: Kilocode VS Code Rules tab resolves Documents folder via `xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS`, which prints bare `$HOME` when no user-dirs config exists (WSL, headless servers, minimal Linux installs), so it reads and writes global rules at `~/Cline/Rules`. SDK rule search paths only covered `~/Documents/Cline/Rules`, so rules written by headless installs never reached system prompt (silently ignored). Fix: add `~/Cline/Rules` to search list before `~/Documents/Cline/Rules`, so both paths are checked.
- **Why**: Headless installs (WSL, SSH, Docker, CI) have no `~/.config/user-dirs.dirs`, so `xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS` returns `$HOME` and rules end up at `~/Cline/Rules` instead of `~/Documents/Cline/Rules`. SDK must search both paths.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13614 (fix(shared): discover global rules at ~/Cline/Rules)
- **Category**: config (rules discovery)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~3h — Alexi src/config/rules.ts L1-187 `loadRules` scans workspace `.alexi/rules/` L34, workspace `.kilo/rules/` L35, and global `~/Documents/alexi/Rules/` L73-75, but has NO `~/.alexi/rules` fallback for headless installs. `xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS` returns `$HOME` when no user-dirs config, so rules written to `~/.alexi/rules` (common in WSL/headless) would be ignored. Add `~/.alexi/rules` as fallback path before `~/Documents/alexi/Rules` in `loadRules` L73. Also check if Alexi TUI/CLI writes global rules to `~/.alexi/rules` or `~/Documents/alexi/Rules` — if it writes to `~/.alexi/rules` by default on headless, that is the primary path and `~/Documents/alexi/Rules` is the fallback, not vice versa. Verify write location and align search path order).

#### 4. Kilocode #13626: Checkpoint workspace restore HEAD validation — refuse restore when commits made after checkpoint (LOW ~8h)

- **What**: Kilocode checkpoint workspace restore runs `git reset --hard`, which moves current branch pointer. If commits were made after checkpoint (by user or agent), the reset silently knocked them off the branch, leaving them reachable only through reflog (data loss). Fix: guard the reset — if HEAD no longer matches the commit the checkpoint was created on, throw descriptive error (including how many commits would be dropped) instead of destroying history. Chat-only restore unaffected. Close the guard-to-reset race with atomic ref update: replace reset's branch move with `git update-ref HEAD <new> <old>` (compare-and-swap), which fails if HEAD no longer points at verified commit, then follow with `git reset --hard` to sync index and worktree to already-moved HEAD.
- **Why**: Checkpoint restore should not silently discard commits made after the checkpoint was created.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13626 (fix(core): refuse checkpoint workspace restore when HEAD moved past the checkpoint)
- **Category**: tool (checkpoint / git)
- **Size**: LOW (~8h — Alexi src/core/checkpoints.ts L1-258 has checkpoint save/restore (`saveCheckpoint` L76-177, `restoreCheckpoint` L179-258). `restoreCheckpoint` L237-242 runs `git reset --hard <commit>` without HEAD validation, would produce same silent commit-drop bug if user made commits after checkpoint. Implement: (1) after loading checkpoint L191-201, run `git rev-parse HEAD` to get current HEAD, (2) if HEAD != checkpoint.commit, count commits between them with `git rev-list --count <checkpoint.commit>..HEAD`, (3) throw descriptive error with commit count, (4) replace `git reset --hard <commit>` L242 with two-phase atomic update: `git update-ref HEAD <checkpoint.commit> <current-head>` (CAS), then `git reset --hard` (no target, sync to current HEAD). Pattern is CLI-portable. However, NO reported user impact, no open issues for this bug. Defer until prioritized).

#### 7. Kilocode #13627: Hub-managed schedule persistence — exempt virtual hub/schedules path from file reconciliation (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Kilocode hub-managed schedules (agent-created routines stored in virtual `hub/schedules` path, not backed by filesystem files) were wiped by cron reconciliation on hub restart. Reconciliation removed specs not present on disk, treating absence as deletion. Fix: exempt specs with virtual `hub/schedules` source path from removal reconciliation. Require recorded source mtime as proof a spec is file-backed before removing it (hub-managed schedules have no mtime). Closes spoof gap where a malicious client could set source path to `hub/schedules` to bypass reconciliation.
- **Why**: Agent-created schedules should survive hub restarts and desktop app updates.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13627 (Fix scheduled tasks disappearing after desktop app updates)
- **Category**: tool (infrastructure / schedules)
- **Size**: LOW (Kilocode hub daemon feature — virtual schedule path, file reconciliation exemption, mtime-based file-backing proof. Alexi has NO hub daemon mode, NO scheduled tasks/routines, NO file reconciliation for virtual resources. Task-scheduler.ts L1-316 persists schedules to filesystem (cron expressions, no virtual paths). Pattern only relevant if Alexi adds hub daemon mode with virtual resources, SKIP for now).

#### 13. Cline #13646: VS Code e2e teardown deadlock fixes — killpg on timeout, disable crash reporter (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Cline VS Code e2e test harness fixes for worker teardown timeouts. Playwright app.close() waits for process exit AND all stdio pipes to close; descendants outliving main process (chrome_crashpad_handler, dconf watch, xdg-open browser handlers, VS Code agent host CLI subprocess) keep pipes open, so app.close() never resolves and worker teardown times out (60s). Fixes: killpg (SIGKILL whole process group / taskkill /T on Windows) when app.close() times out, launch VS Code with --disable-crash-reporter so no crashpad handler survives, seed user-data-dir with `chat.disableAIFeatures: true` so VS Code AI features never start agent host process, drop redundant page.close() that deadlocks on already-exited app, stop opening real external browser in Codex OAuth test (browser is orphaned process holding harness pipes). Also deflake hub daemon e2e on Windows: retry transient handshake failures within 15s budget, raise singleton test timeout to 60s, raise e2e testTimeout to 60s for slow runners spawning two daemons.
- **Why**: VS Code e2e tests should not time out on worker teardown or flake on Windows runners.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13646 (fix(ci): stop e2e worker teardown timeouts and deflake hub daemon e2e on Windows)
- **Category**: tests (harness / e2e)
- **Size**: LOW (Cline VS Code e2e test harness improvements — Playwright app lifecycle, process cleanup, stdio pipe handling, flake mitigation on Windows. Alexi has NO VS Code extension e2e tests (tests/ has unit tests, no e2e Playwright tests). Pattern is test infrastructure, not production code. SKIP).
